name: Focused retry boundary
summary: A retry teaches efficiently when it returns the player near the newest unresolved decision while preserving enough consequence for earlier execution to matter.
player_action: The player fails, restarts, and practices the unresolved section.
system_response: The checkpoint boundary restores a declared state with bounded setup time, resources, and solved prerequisites.

conflicts_with: zero-cost retry that bypasses the tested resource decision

failure_modes: Solved traversal dominates time before the unsolved rule.
The restored resource state changes the intended decision.
The checkpoint skips a dependency needed to understand failure.
Instant retries remove every meaningful consequence.
accessibility: Offer practice and reduced-repetition options separately from difficulty.
Do not require repeated unskippable presentation before control returns.

smallest_playable_test.setup: A three-stage encounter where stages one and two can become solved while stage three remains unsolved; compare start, midpoint, and immediate retry boundaries.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: The boundary minimizes non-learning repetition without changing the unresolved decision or eliminating consequence.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: Learning accelerates but tension or resource meaning collapses.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Most retry time repeats already-solved content or restored state invalidates comparison.

evidence.claim: Bandai Namco presents Dark Souls Remastered as a world of challenge, discovery, and repeated mastery supported by bonfire-based progression.
evidence.game_version: Dark Souls Remastered official product page
evidence.notes: Supports studying retry position as part of challenge and world traversal.
